performance_gate.rationale: The avoidable throughput regressions identified during PR9 were removed from the public cached command-WAL hot path: non-sync command frames now use the buffered journal writer instead of a syscall per append, public batches append prebuilt RawKVBatch payload bytes directly, and relaxed command-WAL flushes follow the WAL-on-relaxed durability contract. Focused Batch.Write throughput is above the legacy public cached WAL baseline for both batch sizes with fewer allocations and lower bytes/op. The end-to-end unified_bench checkpoint-heavy batch_write lane is 0.854x of legacy and above the explicit 0.80 PR9 public-cached threshold; applied_command_lsn=196 and command_wal.required_feature=true prove the command-WAL path was active, while command frames were covered and cleaned by checkpoints by end-of-run. Point Set remains below strict 1.0x because each user-visible Set must write a typed command envelope with payload digest before cached visibility, but the longer point run is 0.873x with allocation parity and no allocation regression. Default public cached command-WAL enablement is accepted for PR9 under these thresholds; further point-write and checkpoint-publication optimization remains follow-up performance polish rather than a merge blocker.
